producer_report.summary: Root cause: reading acceptance (`check_reading_acceptance` in athena-core `reading.rs`) had no mapping from a request's outcome to governance files. A reading for "publish to GitHub Pages" without a workflow, or a new config section without `athena.toml`, was accepted, and the gap showed up only at admission after the producer had finished. I added `check_governance_coverage` to `check_reading_acceptance`. It runs for first attempts and retries alike and makes no model call. It reuses admission's `is_governance` and `governance_change_is_listed`. It refuses a reading when (a) a governance deliverable is not named by any criterion, (b) `crates/athena-data/src/config.rs` is listed without `athena.toml`, or (c) the request contains a keyword from a small table and the matching governance file is neither listed and named nor named in `out_of_scope`. The table has two mappings: workflow, CI, deploy, GitHub Pages and similar words map to `.github/workflows/`; routing, checks, classes, budgets, gate and configuration map to `athena.toml`. There are also exact-filename entries for `defaults.toml`, `rust-toolchain` and `setup.sh`. The refusal names each missing path and why, and says to list it as a deliverable and name it in a criterion, or put it in `out_of_scope`. I added a doc comment to `admission.rs`, a CHANGELOG entry and a paragraph in `docs/architecture.md`. No prompt files changed.

checks_run.note: 12 passed; the boundary-word scan is clean.

criteria_check.criterion: The change description names the root cause: reading acceptance has no mapping from the request's outcome to governance files, so the omission is found only at admission. The fix is in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs `check_reading_acceptance`, called for first attempts and retries alike, not in any one job's reading.
criteria_check.evidence: The doc comment on `check_governance_coverage` in reading.rs and the new CHANGELOG entry both name that root cause. `check_reading_acceptance` now calls it, and the test `the_governance_check_applies_to_a_retry_as_to_a_first_attempt` passes.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: new tests in reading.rs fail without the change and pass with it. A reading for the request 'Publish to GitHub Pages' with no workflow deliverable is refused, naming .github/workflows. A reading that lists athena.toml but no criterion names it is refused. A reading that lists crates/athena-data/src/config.rs without athena.toml is refused. Each of these readings is accepted once it lists and names the file, or names it in out_of_scope. A request with no matching keywords and no governance deliverables is accepted unchanged.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core` gave 541 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. The new tests are `a_reading_for_publish_to_github_pages_without_a_workflow_is_refused`, `a_listed_governance_file_must_be_named_by_a_criterion_whatever_the_request_says`, `a_new_config_section_needs_athena_toml_listed_and_named` and `a_request_without_governance_keywords_or_deliverables_is_accepted_unchanged`. Each asserts the refusal and then acceptance after listing and naming the file or naming it in out_of_scope. They call `check_reading_acceptance`, which accepted all these readings before the change, so they fail without it. I did not run them against the base to confirm.

criteria_check.criterion: The new tests are table-driven over the keyword table, covering the class (several request phrasings such as CI, gate, workflow, routing, budgets, classes), not just the three recorded jobs. Run `cargo test -p athena-core` to check.

For each it checks refusal, listed-but-unnamed refusal, acceptance when listed and named, and acceptance when out of scope. It passes.

open_issues: The keyword match is a heuristic. Ordinary requests that mention words like "checks", "config" or "CI" now need an explicit decision on athena.toml or workflows. That costs the reader one retry, as the reading accepted for this job expected.
The email-address finding from job 20261015-014012-akwq is a separate policy matter and was left alone, as the reading said.
mistakes: My first keyword table had broad words (defaults, installer, check, class, route). I narrowed it to the specified phrases and exact filenames before running the tests, because those words appear in many ordinary requests.
learnings: `has_phrase` in reading.rs treats '_' as a word boundary, so "athena_gate" would match "gate". The new check swaps '_' for a letter before matching, so identifiers do not trigger keywords.
The keyword check needs the reading to have at least one deliverable, a capability and no question. Declined, asking and no-change readings are not refused for a missing governance file.
Admission's `governance_change_is_listed` matches a criterion by full path or by file name, so a criterion that says "pages.yml deploys the site" names `.github/workflows/pages.yml`.
